THE PROBLEM LIES IN `astropy/modeling/separable.py`, SPECIFICALLY IN THE `_separable` FUNCTION THAT HANDLES COMPOUND MODELS WITH THE `&` OPERATOR.

WHEN PROCESSING NESTED COMPOUND MODELS, THE CODE FAILS TO PROPERLY PROPAGATE THE SEPARABILITY MATRIX OF THE NESTED MODEL. INSTEAD OF PRESERVING THE INTERNAL SEPARABILITY STRUCTURE, IT TREATS THE NESTED COMPOUND MODEL AS A SINGLE OPAQUE UNIT.

THE ISSUE IS IN THE `_cstack` FUNCTION (AROUND LINE 212-242). WHEN COMBINING SEPARABILITY MATRICES FOR THE `&` OPERATOR, THE CODE ASSUMES IT IS WORKING WITH SIMPLE MODELS. FOR A NESTED COMPOUND MODEL LIKE `cm = Linear1D & Linear1D`, THE FUNCTION SHOULD RECURSIVELY OBTAIN ITS SEPARABILITY MATRIX. INSTEAD, IT APPEARS TO BE CALLING `_coord_matrix` DIRECTLY ON THE COMPOUND MODEL, WHICH RETURNS AN INCORRECT FULLY-COUPLED MATRIX.

```python
def _separable(transform):

        return _operators[transform.op](sepleft, sepright, transform)

```
